One of the five holiest Jain pilgrimage sites: Dharna Shah built it after a divine vision of a celestial vehicle (Nalini-Gulma Vimana design), under Mewar king Rana Kumbha. The chaumukha (four-faced) Adinath idol faces all four cardinal directions; famous 'forest of pillars' - 1444 intricately carved marble pillars, no two alike, positioned so none blocks the deity; 29 halls, 80 domes, Maru-Gurjara architecture. Coordinates are a district-level map match; Wikipedia lists 25.1157444, 73.4728306 for the temple (verify).

name: Ranakpur Jain Temple (Chaumukha / Adinatha Temple)
town_description: Ranakpur is a village in Pali district, Rajasthan, in a secluded Aravalli valley about 90 km from Udaipur. It is home to the celebrated 15th-century Jain temple complex (the Chaumukha/Adinath temple and satellite shrines including Neminath, Parshwanath, Surya and Amba), one of the five holiest Jain pilgrimage sites, in the Gorwad Panch Tirth circuit.
